newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria reports big budget surplus in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria reports big budget surplus in 1996.

text.p: Nigeria's military ruler General Sani Abacha said on Saturday his government recorded a budget surplus of 37 billion naira in 1996 compared with only one billion naira in the preceeding year.
In a radio and television broadcast of the 1997 fiscal budget, Abacha said the 1996 surplus amounted to 1.45 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).

"This is no mean achievement, considering that in 1995, a modest surplus of only one billion naira or 0.06 percent of GDP was accomplished, while there was, in fact, a huge deficit of 81 billion naira in 1994," he said.
The military government has been widely credited with more financial discipline in the last two years when economic reforms appear to have taken firmer root in Nigeria.
Abacha said the surplus in 1996 would be re-channelled this year into productive sectors of the economy, especially in rural areas, to improve living standards there.
